explain.say: On 31 October 1517 a monk and professor in Wittenberg, Martin Luther, sent ninety-five theses, points for debate, attacking the sale of indulgences: payments believed to reduce punishment for sins after death. Whether he really nailed them to a church door is still debated. Within a few years Western Christianity had split. Look at the timeline.

explain.say: Why so fast? See the causes. First, the printing press, invented in Mainz about seventy years earlier. Luther wrote short, punchy pamphlets in German, and printers sold them in huge numbers. He became the best-selling author of his age. Which cause do you think a prince cared about most?

explain.say: Look at the map. From Wittenberg, reform spread to Swiss cities, where Zwingli led in Zurich and Calvin later in Geneva. In England, Henry VIII broke with Rome in 1534, largely to end his marriage. Rome stayed the centre of Catholic Christianity. How did politics and faith mix in Henry's case?

Wars followed. In 1555 the Peace of Augsburg let each German prince choose Catholic or Lutheran faith for his lands. Meanwhile the Council of Trent, from 1545, reformed Catholic teaching and training of priests, the Catholic Reformation. Why might letting rulers choose religion keep a fragile peace?

faq.a: Long-standing criticism of Church abuses such as the sale of indulgences, new humanist study of the Bible, Luther's theology of salvation by faith, the printing press, and the political interests of princes and cities.

faq.q: Why did the Reformation spread so quickly?
faq.a: Printing let Luther's German pamphlets reach huge audiences; preachers and town councils adopted reform; and princes saw advantages in controlling the Church and its lands.

faq.q: What was the Peace of Augsburg?
faq.a: A 1555 settlement in the Holy Roman Empire letting each prince choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his territory, summed up later in the phrase cuius regio, eius religio: whose realm, his religion.
asks: What does cuius regio eius religio mean?

faq.q: What was the Council of Trent?
faq.a: A Catholic council held between 1545 and 1563 that restated Catholic doctrine, rejected Protestant teachings and reformed the training and discipline of clergy, a key part of the Catholic Reformation.

faq.q: Did Luther really nail the theses to a door?
faq.a: We know he sent them to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz on 31 October 1517. The story of nailing them to the castle church door comes from later accounts, and historians still debate it.

facts: Luther's Ninety-five Theses are dated 31 October 1517.
The Peace of Augsburg was agreed in 1555.
The Council of Trent met between 1545 and 1563.
